reference.title: Monitoring repository mirroring
reference.shortdesc: Red Hat Quay exposes Prometheus metrics and a health API endpoint for repository mirroring. Use these tools to monitor synchronization progress, detect failures, and configure alerts in Prometheus or Grafana.

section.p: Metrics are published from the mirror worker process through the existing Prometheus push gateway (typically port 9091). The health API endpoint reads repository state from the database and, when available, worker metrics from the in-process Prometheus registry.

section.title: Repository mirror Prometheus metrics
section.p: The following table describes the primary repository mirroring metrics added in Red Hat Quay 3.18.

entry.p: Number of tags pending synchronization. Labels: namespace, repository.
Status of the last synchronization attempt. Labels: namespace, repository, last_error_reason. Values: 0 (failed), 1 (success), 2 (in progress). Use last_error_reason="" for per-repository counts.
Whether all tags synchronized in the last run. Labels: namespace, repository. Values: 0 (incomplete), 1 (complete).
Cumulative synchronization failures. Labels: namespace, reason.
Set to 1 while a mirror worker process is running. Sum across worker targets for total active workers.
Unix timestamp when the last sync attempt started. Labels: namespace, repository.
Sync operation duration aggregated by namespace.
Number of repositories not yet mirrored. Maintained for backward compatibility.

section.title: Repository mirror health endpoint
section.p: Red Hat Quay exposes two health endpoints for repository mirroring:

ul.li: GET /api/v1/repository/mirror/health — namespace-scoped or global health. Without namespace, the caller must be a superuser with full access. With namespace, organization members can query their organization, and user-namespace owners or user administrators can query that namespace.
GET /api/v1/superuser/mirror/health — global summary for superusers, without repository-identifying issue samples.

section.p: Both endpoints require a fresh login. A validated OAuth or SSO token satisfies the check. A password-based browser session must be within FRESH_LOGIN_TIMEOUT (default: 10m).
The responses include overall health, worker status, repository counts, pending tags, and any detected issues. HTTP 200 means healthy; HTTP 503 means unhealthy.

ul.li: namespace — limit results to one namespace
limit and offset — paginate detailed results

section.p: For endpoint parameters, response schema, and authorization requirements, see getRepositoryMirrorHealth and getSuperUserRepositoryMirrorHealth.
